title: no verb repairs an unreadable search-index table in place: intent index rebuild opens the store through the same read it would repair
body:
Split out of 0447 by vc on 2026-09-18, for the line after the close-out. Found by dc driving 0447's remedy before building it.

## What was driven

Installed pair 493705d98 (SQLite 3.53.2), a scratch project under an isolated HOME, one thread, a warm store. Then `doc_sections` was replaced by a plain table (`DROP TABLE doc_sections; CREATE TABLE doc_sections (unrelated TEXT);`). Every verb below refused in the open-time ingest with the same error, because each opens the store through `Store::doc_sections`:

    intent search hello        rc 1  could not read the committed canon
    intent index rebuild       rc 1  (the same)
    intent st list             rc 1  (the same)
    intent backup              rc 1  (the same)
    intent backup --list       (the same error)
    intent doctor              rc 0  0 finding(s)

0447 fixes what those say and makes `doctor` count it. It does not make any of them work.

## The defect this issue owns

**No verb repairs an unreadable search-index table in place.** `intent index rebuild` is the obvious door, and it is behind the same wall: it cannot run until the read it would repair succeeds. The only way out today is by hand -- restore a snapshot, or rebuild the store -- and neither has a verb: `intent backup` is one-way ("no restore verb ships"), and the store's own remedy says never to delete it, correctly, because it is the source of truth.

## The fix, as far as it can be sized from here (S to M)

`intent index rebuild` must be able to run when an index table cannot be read. It opens the store without reading the prose sections, drops and recreates the fts5 tables from the schema, and re-indexes from the tree. Sections are derived, so nothing is lost. When it lands, 0447's remedy names it; the remedy's "No verb in this build repairs it in place" sentence is the line to change, and 0447's arms say where.

## Reach, stated honestly

The injected fault is the only reproduction. The field shapes that would break this SELECT are a schema written by another build, or page-level corruption of the content table, and neither has been observed on a live estate. 0442's damage lived in the index segments, which this SELECT does not read. This is a door with no known traffic yet, which is why vc put it after the close-out rather than in 0447.



CLOSED 2026-09-19, by the landing at fa4841fd3 on vc's GO (T2, patch-id a533ba6d7d19, judged green on top of T1 at fb80369ab: intentsvcs 1807 passed 0 failed, intent-cli 1034 passed 0 failed). `intent index rebuild` now opens through `Facade::open_as(.., Opening::RepairingIndex)`. It reads every other table first, then drops and recreates `doc_sections` and `src_sections` from the store's own DDL in one transaction, then refills the prose. There is no new verb. Refusals: a store that cannot be opened refuses as before; an unreadable table other than the two index tables stops the repair with "nothing was dropped or changed"; a drop, recreate or read-back SQLite refuses rolls back and leaves the store as found. Driven on the worktree build against the injected fault: before, search, st list and backup exited 1; after `index rebuild` (exit 0), search found the issue body and st list, backup and doctor exited 0. 0447's remedy now names `intent index rebuild`. The refusal that a recreated table still cannot be read has no arm, because no fault reproduces it.
